facts.fact: The consolidated text of the Cybercrimes Act (Cap. 443, Revised Edition 2023, originally Act No. 14 of 2015) states it commenced on 1 September 2015 under GN No. 528 of 2015 and applies to Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, criminalising illegal access, interception, data interference, fraud and forgery.

The ICT Minister said on 19 August 2026 that section 29 of the Cybercrimes Act provides a fine of not less than 100m/- or three times the damage, imprisonment of at least five years, or both, for damaging critical ICT infrastructure.

facts.fact: The report cites the Cybercrimes Act (2015) among the instruments behind the country's cybersecurity standing.
Tanzania Police Force reported 745 cybercrime cases for January to June 2026, up from 497 a year earlier, without naming the law they were recorded under.
The Ministry says the government enacted the Cyber Crime Act, 2015 under the RCIP project.

Tanzania's Cybercrimes Act, 2015 (Act No. 14 of 2015) was published as an Act Supplement to the Gazette on 22 May 2015, with offences such as illegal access and interception; it comes into operation on a date the Minister appoints by notice, which the text does not give.
